Answer: A
Reason: The radiograph demonstrates the classic "sandstorm" appearance of pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis, characterized by bilateral, diffuse, fine calcific micronodules that are densely packed in the mid-to-lower zones with relative sparing of the upper lobes (particularly evident on the left). This specific distribution and texture distinguish it from the apical predominance of sarcoidosis or TB, the linear patterns of amyloidosis, or the nodular/reticular patterns of pneumoconiosis.
